definitions.explanation: A substance formed when two or more chemical elements are bonded together in a fixed ratio. Distinguished from mixtures, where components are not chemically bonded.

examples.japanese: {水|みず}は{化合物|かごうぶつ}です。
この{化合物|かごうぶつ}は{二|ふた}つの{元素|げんそ}からできている。
examples.english: This compound is made up of two elements.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{化合物|かごうぶつ}を{合成|ごうせい}するために、{研究者|けんきゅうしゃ}たちは{何年|なんねん}も{実験|じっけん}を{続|つづ}けた。
examples.english: The researchers continued experimenting for years to synthesize a new compound.

notes:
Composed of {化合|かごう} (chemical combination) + {物|ぶつ} (substance). A fundamental term in chemistry education, encountered from middle school science onward in Japan.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有機|ゆうき}{化合物|かごうぶつ}: organic compound
- {無機|むき}{化合物|かごうぶつ}: inorganic compound
- {化合物|かごうぶつ}を{合成|ごうせい}する: synthesize a compound
- {化学|かがく}{化合物|かごうぶつ}: chemical compound

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {混合物|こんごうぶつ}: mixture — components are not chemically bonded and can be separated physically
- {元素|げんそ}: element — a pure substance consisting of one type of atom
- {分子|ぶんし}: molecule — the smallest unit of a compound that retains its chemical properties
